items.title: Quantum trade moves beyond science fiction: AlphaCheck
items.summary: Two newly public quantum computing companies are about to report earnings. Their results will test the appetite for the budding technology that has captivated some corners of Wall Street.

items.title: This AI Stock Is Surging. Can It Shake the ‘Meme Stock’ Label?
items.summary: Applied Optoelectronics reports solid earnings, giving a boost to investors who hope it can be more than a meme stock.

items.title: What Is The Market Really Expecting From AVGO Stock?
items.summary: At $422, Broadcom (AVGO) is being priced to deliver 26% revenue growth annually for the next 5 years simply to defend today's 68.4x multiple. That sits below the 32% the business is currently growing at, which is the unusual part. The multiple has already priced in a slowdown that has not yet appeared.

items.title: The Options Market Says Marvell Stock Could Halve Or More Than Double
items.summary: This band is not a panic premium; it sits close to what the stock has actually delivered over the past year, and a holder carries every bit of that width.

items.title: Is Broadcom’s (AVGO) Next Big Bet Hidden in Plain Sight?
items.summary: On August 4, Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) said its software business had joined NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) and other industry partners as a founding member of the Open Secure AI Alliance, an effort to build open, collaborative defenses against AI-driven cyberattacks. items.title: Are Wall Street Analysts Predicting Broadcom Stock Will Climb or Sink?
items.summary: As Broadcom has outperformed the SPX over the past year, Wall Street analysts maintain a bullish outlook on the stock’s prospects.

items.title: This Is Where Nvidia Beats Broadcom
items.summary: Nvidia and Broadcom both posted staggering AI revenue this quarter, but one strategy bets on a handful of hyperscalers while the other bets on every model builder alive. The divergence between those bets reveals a quiet but widening competitive gap.

items.title: Broadcom Can Eat Nvidia’s Lunch Just Like This
items.summary: NVIDIA posted the largest data center quarter in history, yet one rival is growing AI revenue faster and quietly locking up the customers who matter most. The custom silicon war is already underway, and the scoreboard looks nothing like the headlines.
